name: Castello
tagline: The walled citadel on the ridge, with the towers
description: The medieval quarter on the limestone ridge above the city, enclosed by Pisan walls with the Elephant and San Pancrazio towers you can climb, the cathedral and the archaeological museum holding the Nuragic bronzes. Lifts and a funicular help with the height. It is the most striking place to live in Cagliari.
bestFor: Stays that want the citadel, the museum and the views
pros: Views over the gulf and the salt pans
The cathedral, the towers and the museum together
cons: Steep, with lifts doing the work
The stone walls defeat domestic wifi hardware

name: Marina
tagline: The old port quarter, narrow streets and the best eating
description: The quarter running from Castello down to the harbour, a dense grid of narrow streets holding most of the city's restaurants, bars and small hotels. It is busy year-round rather than only in season, and it is where the evening happens. Housing is old apartments above the trade.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the restaurants and bars downstairs
pros: The densest run of restaurants and bars in the city
Central for the port, Castello and the station
Lively all year rather than seasonally

name: Poetto and Quartu
tagline: The eight-kilometre city beach and the flamingo pans
description: The beach running eight kilometres along the eastern edge of the city towards Quartu, with kiosks and beach clubs along it, and the Molentargius salt pans behind holding a resident flamingo population inside the municipal boundary. It is a fifteen-minute bus from the centre.
bestFor: Stays that want the beach and the salt pans on the doorstep
pros: Flamingos in the salt pans behind
Fifteen minutes by bus to the centre
cons: Quieter and partly closed in winter

name: Villanova and San Benedetto
tagline: The residential centre, with the covered market
description: The nineteenth-century districts east of Castello, holding the San Benedetto market, one of the largest covered markets in Italy, along with ordinary apartment buildings, everyday shops and a settled local population. It is central, practical and cheaper than the historic quarters.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting the market and a normal neighbourhood
pros: San Benedetto market for produce and fish
Central and flat, unlike the citadel

name: Chia and the Southern Coast (50 km southwest)
tagline: The dune beaches and the Sulcis coast
description: The coast running southwest from the city towards Chia and Teulada, with dune-backed beaches, a Spanish watchtower on the headland and water that is among the clearest in the Mediterranean. It is largely undeveloped and requires a car, with the road running through low hills.
bestFor: Stays wanting the best beaches on the island with the city an hour away
pros: Among the finest beaches in the Mediterranean
Dunes, watchtowers and largely no development
cons: Fifty kilometres from Cagliari and a car is essential
Very few services along the coast
Busy in August with Italian holidaymakers
